items.h: New housing report exposes the gap between Rhode Island incomes and home prices
items.sum: Newport’s median single-family price reached $1.51 million in the report’s 2025 data, requiring an estimated $459,600 income to buy affordably.

items.h: Voters face $600 million in statewide borrowing questions
items.sum: Five ballot measures cover higher education, housing, economic development, arts and culture, and clean energy.

items.h: NOAA’s Atlantic operations center is preparing to open in Newport
items.sum: The $147 million Naval Station complex is scheduled to be fully operational by late January 2027, bringing shoreside jobs and research activity.

items.h: URI announces an interdisciplinary artificial-intelligence degree
items.sum: The new bachelor’s program combines applied AI with ethics, safety, and responsible implementation through business and arts-and-sciences collaboration.

items.h: Merlin moves flight-testing operations from Quonset to Smithfield
items.sum: The autonomous-flight company says North Central State Airport offers additional hangar space for its expanding fleet and testing programs.

items.h: Westerly remembers attorney and former legislator Peter Lewiss
items.sum: Community members are honoring his work in public service, the arts, and animal welfare following his death at 59.

items.h: Newport County holiday-assistance registration is open
items.sum: The MLK Community Center is accepting in-person applications for holiday food and children’s gifts; Thanksgiving registration ends November 13.

items.h: Twenty-seven employers are expected at Newport’s November 5 career fair
items.sum: Innovate Newport will host recruiters from manufacturing, government, health care, and other sectors between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m.

items.h: Rhode Island documentary “The Pizza Principal” announces its premiere
items.sum: Filmmaker Kirk Benttinen’s November 20 Providence screening will introduce the film alongside shorts through his RI Docs project.

items.h: I-195 will close in both directions for bridge demolition November 6–7
items.sum: RIDOT plans a closure near East Providence’s Taunton Avenue interchange beginning at 10 p.m. Friday, with all lanes expected to reopen by noon Saturday.

items.h: Rhode Island’s governor race enters its final stretch
items.sum: Helena Foulkes, Ken Block, and Aaron Guckian delivered their closing arguments in the final televised debate ahead of the November 3 election.

items.h: New state assistance could lower health insurance costs for thousands
items.sum: HealthSource RI enrollment opens November 1; the new RIMAP program is expected to help more than 20,000 eligible customers afford 2027 coverage.

items.h: Winter electric bills rise, with refunds and discounts changing the total
items.sum: Rhode Island Energy’s seasonal increases began October 1, alongside refunds; additional discounts are scheduled for early 2027.

items.h: Neronha prepares a proposal for a public health insurance option
items.sum: The attorney general’s planned announcement includes restructuring state health oversight and creating a state-run insurance option.

items.h: Tiverton advances public water connections for homes with contaminated wells
items.sum: Six households are targeted for connections; officials reported that 110 of nearly 200 tested wells were contaminated with PFAS.

items.h: Hasbro CEO’s comments provoke backlash as the company leaves Pawtucket
items.sum: Governor McKee joined local criticism of remarks about Rhode Island as Hasbro prepares to complete its move to Boston.

items.h: Providence superintendent reportedly negotiates an exit
items.sum: Reporting that Javier Montañez is discussing departure comes amid senior leadership turnover; the district has declined to comment on personnel matters.

items.h: Westerly Hospital patients face uncertainty over UnitedHealthcare negotiations
items.sum: Its parent system is negotiating a new contract. The insurer says in-network treatment will continue through January 3, 2027, even without an agreement.

items.h: Rhode Island’s falling unemployment rate comes with a warning
items.sum: RIPEC and Bryant researchers say the improvement reflects people leaving the workforce, complicating the picture of the state’s economy.

items.h: Costco selects Smithfield for its proposed first Rhode Island store
items.sum: The Route 116 location remains subject to approvals, with a proposed 2028 opening and more than 200 potential jobs.

items.h: Early voting surges as ballot-return deadlines approach
items.sum: Participation during the first ten days was 88% above the comparable 2022 period. Mail ballots must arrive by 8 p.m. November 3.

items.h: Providence parents challenge the district’s AI reading program
items.sum: Concerns about AMIRA include consent, student recordings, privacy, and children with speech differences. District officials say new voice recordings are not retained.

items.h: Rhode Island’s new license-plate camera safeguards remain voluntary
items.sum: McKee’s Flock camera guidelines leave unresolved questions about enforceability and privacy while the pause on new installations continues.

items.h: The General Assembly plans a post-election return
items.sum: Lawmakers are expected to consider judicial appointments, potentially including McKee’s Supreme Court selection, in the first such session in six years.

items.h: Providence moves forward with major school consolidation plans
items.sum: Proposed pairings include Young Woods with Roger Williams and Carnevale with DelSesto, affecting school assignments, facilities, and neighborhood expectations.

items.h: Providence School Board postpones a vote on removing its president
items.sum: Members delayed action until November 18 while reviewing bylaws and pursuing a process to repair working relationships.

items.h: Edesia expands its North Kingstown factory and adds jobs
items.sum: The nutrition nonprofit opened 215,000 square feet of additional space, expanding production capacity following disruptions to federal aid funding.

items.h: Large trucks are now restricted on part of Greenville Avenue in Smithfield
items.sum: New signs follow findings that large trucks could not negotiate a turn without mounting the sidewalk.

items.h: Kristin Sousa takes over as interim health and human services secretary
items.sum: The Medicaid director’s appointment begins October 29 following Richard Charest’s departure from the cabinet position.

items.h: Westerly’s property-tax assessment appeal deadline is today
items.sum: The town’s calendar lists October 29 as the deadline to file assessment appeals.

items.h: Four candidates compete in Senate District 17
items.sum: Republican Thomas Paolino faces Democrat Nelly Burdette and independents John Barr and Jina Petrarca in the district spanning parts of Lincoln, North Smithfield, and North Providence.

items.h: Megan Cotter faces Jasmin Roy in House District 39
items.sum: The western Rhode Island contest centers on affordability, education, local control, and balancing development with rural preservation.

items.h: Woonsocket’s mayoral race focuses on leadership and redevelopment
items.sum: Candidates are debating City Hall management, downtown investment, paving, and how to move stalled properties forward.

items.h: Write-in campaigns shape a Cumberland Fire Committee contest
items.sum: Incumbent Paul Santoro joined the District 2 write-in race after not filing through the normal ballot process.

items.h: Five candidates seek four South Kingstown School Committee seats
items.sum: Enrollment losses, spending, educational equity, and competition with other school options are central issues.

items.h: Westerly’s School Committee election puts performance and leadership in focus
items.sum: Six candidates are competing for three seats, with only one incumbent in the field.

items.h: Westerly voters will decide four town charter amendments
items.sum: Questions address filling elected vacancies, School Committee term limits, and how the town publishes ordinance notices.

items.h: RIC launches Whipple Hall’s cybersecurity-focused renovation
items.sum: The project will create a home for its Institute for Cybersecurity and Emerging Technologies, following voter approval of a $73 million bond.

items.h: URI students and employees get statewide RIPTA rides at no cost
items.sum: The new U-Pass agreement allows enrolled students, faculty, and staff to use university identification for unlimited bus travel.

items.h: Central Falls teacher Briana Jones wins a $25,000 Milken award
items.sum: She becomes the city’s first recipient of the national educator recognition.

items.h: North Providence negotiates over its former public safety complex
items.sum: The developer and town representatives are discussing a possible compromise after years of disagreement; the property’s future use remains unsettled.

items.h: Woonsocket’s vacant former school moves toward residential redevelopment
items.sum: A groundbreaking marked progress on the Residences at Park Place. Published unit counts differ, so the final scale remains worth checking.

items.h: A Rhode Island design competition aims to make accessory homes more affordable
items.sum: The +1 RI ADU initiative targets design costs associated with adding smaller homes to existing properties.

items.h: Westerly’s Tower Street center prepares for education and health services
items.sum: Nursing-assistant training, GED preparation, and a planned Wood River Health presence are part of the former school’s new role.

items.h: Westerly approves $710,000 for school maintenance projects
items.sum: The allocation covers roof, flooring, and window work after debate about the district’s reserves and capital budgeting.

items.h: Smith Hill is getting solar carports, batteries, and EV charging infrastructure
items.sum: State energy officials announced projects costing approximately $9 million, with construction expected to begin in 2027.
items.outlet: Rhode Island Office of Energy Resources

items.h: Rhode Island Energy begins an $8.2 million Middletown upgrade
items.sum: The utility is replacing 65 aging wooden transmission structures with steel monopoles to improve reliability.

items.h: Shellfishermen warn about declining quahog stocks and catches
items.sum: Reporting examines shrinking landings and changing conditions in Narragansett Bay, with consequences for working fishermen and a signature Rhode Island food.

items.h: Aquidneck Island’s long-discussed rail-with-trail project advances
items.sum: Partners are developing a path alongside the Newport Secondary corridor and seeking public input, including a November 1 community train ride.

items.h: Burrillville faces questions about costs after an anti-SLAPP ruling
items.sum: Residents are asking who will pay legal fees and damages sought following the town’s unsuccessful claim against a synthetic-turf opponent.

items.h: Narrow River dredging will miss the current season, town manager says
items.sum: Funding and scheduling problems could push Narragansett’s project into the next available work window.

items.h: Charlestown asks RIDOT to address Old Post Road bicycle safety
items.sum: The council approved a field meeting to consider signage and possible pavement markings along the proposed coastal bike route.

items.h: Officials lift the harmful-algae advisory at Cranston’s Blackamore Pond
items.sum: Recent testing found low algae levels and no detected toxins, allowing the recreational advisory to be withdrawn.

items.h: Traditional snow days return in Tiverton schools
items.sum: The School Committee voted to discontinue electronic learning days for weather closures, with missed time made up when necessary.

items.h: Barrington bans e-bikes and e-scooters from sidewalks and parks
items.sum: The council unanimously expanded an existing ordinance; the change took effect October 5.

items.h: Rhode Island Life Science Hub signs a regional biobank agreement
items.sum: The partnership will plan how Rhode Island hospitals can contribute samples and data for research, initially emphasizing Alzheimer’s and other brain diseases.

items.h: Cranston memory-care community changes ownership
items.sum: Wingate Living acquired Victoria Court and renamed the 65-unit facility Wingate Residences at Cranston.

items.h: Bradley Hospital appoints a new chief medical officer
items.sum: Dr. Chase Samsel joins the East Providence children’s psychiatric hospital from Boston Children’s Hospital.

items.h: Rhode Island health leaders warn that access remains unequal
items.sum: At a Warwick summit, participants highlighted affordability, provider availability, and federal policy uncertainty affecting local patients.

items.h: Westerly Hospital receives $100,000 for treatment rooms
items.sum: Westerly Community Credit Union’s donation supports improvements to local hospital care.

items.h: ServeRI distributes $1.45 million in AmeriCorps grants
items.sum: Eight Rhode Island organizations will support 140 service members working on education, housing, workforce development, and environmental needs.

items.h: Pawtucket nonprofit receives funding for nursing-assistant training at no tuition cost
items.sum: Harbor of Hope’s $30,000 Rhode Island Foundation grant supports training, certification preparation, and job-placement assistance.

items.h: A new Smithfield swim school targets an early-2027 opening
items.sum: The Cove Swim School plans lessons for children and adults, including quieter sessions for swimmers who benefit from reduced stimulation.

items.h: Wakefield’s Looney Tunes II will close after more than 50 years
items.sum: The record store plans to shut its doors November 30; nearby gift shop Nico Scout also plans to close its storefront.

items.h: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Rhode Island marks 60 years
items.sum: Its anniversary breakfast in Lincoln raised more than $100,000 for mentoring programs.

items.h: Newport preservation projects receive Rhody Awards recognition
items.sum: Honorees include Castle Hill’s fire restoration, a lead-paint guidance project, and Salve Regina’s Michael Semenza; public voting continues through noon October 30.

items.h: Newport sailor Ben Rosenberg joins America’s Cup challenger ARC Team USA
items.sum: The local sailor will serve as an AC75 sailor and coaching-support analyst for the American campaign.
